text:
mira: Noticed a funky installer behavior on a fresh Win11 VM — the MSI placed profiles under %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Redwood\\profiles but redwoodctl (and localserve) look in %APPDATA%\\redwoodctl\\profiles. login says OK, but local testing fails with 401 when trying to use the profile.

sam: can you show `redwoodctl config get profiles.path` and your %APPDATA% value?

mira: sure, pasted below:
```
C:\\> redwoodctl config get profiles.path
C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Roaming\\redwoodctl\\profiles

C:\\> echo %APPDATA%
C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Roaming
```
I can confirm the token file is actually in LocalAppData: C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Local\\Redwood\\profiles\\default\\token.json

devon: that explains it. Installer authoring used LOCALAPPDATA but our CLI and docs assume APPDATA (Roaming). The easiest immediate check: `redwoodctl auth status --profile=default` and `type "C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Local\\Redwood\\profiles\\default\\token.json"` to make sure token shape is OK.

mira: ran both, output: 
```
> redwoodctl auth status --profile=default
Authenticated: true
Expires: 2026-06-11T10:22:54Z

> type C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Local\\Redwood\\profiles\\default\\token.json
{"access_token":"ya29.A0AfH6SM...","expiry":"2026-06-11T10:22:54Z"}
```

sam: token looks fine. So two concurrent problems: installer writes to LocalAppData and CLI expects Roaming. Likely packaging constant mixup.

kevin: from packaging POV we swapped a constant when generating the MSI — will bisect the build scripts. For immediate mitigation we can either set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR env var or make a symlink from Roaming path pointing to LocalAppData. Example: 
```
setx REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR "C:\\Users\\Mira\\AppData\\Local\\Redwood\\profiles"
# restart shell
```

mira: setx worked for me, localserve picks up the token now. thanks. :tada: 

ops: going to open a tracked issue and a small installer patch. QA checklist: fresh install, upgrade paths, per-user vs machine install, and ensure we don't clobber existing tokens. Also confirm behavior when profiles.dir is set via env.

kevin: Created CM-482: "Windows MSI writes profiles to LocalAppData instead of Roaming (%APPDATA%)". Patch branch: installer/msi-fix-profiles.

devon: quick follow-up — there's also a headless auth edge on CI images where `redwoodctl auth login --headless` prints the device code URL but then attempts to open a browser and errors out in environments without shell helpers. Headless should just print the URL and exit (no browser spawn).

sam: logged CM-483: "headless login should not attempt to open browser in non-interactive environments".

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: installer/msi-fix-profiles -> canary windows at 2026-02-12T03:00Z

mira: happy to validate the canary once it lands. will report back with results.

kevin: thanks — we'll keep this thread updated. If anyone hits related problems on mac or Linux packaging, ping here and we'll audit platform-specific paths.

mira: also note for release notes: document REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR env var and the temporary symlink workaround so devs running local testing know the fix.

kevin: noted for changelog. closing loop after canary validation. :white_check_mark:
